subject: Tri-region staggered provisioning playbook request
messages:
From: Sara Nakamura <sara.nakamura@helix.ai>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@helix.ai, ops@helix.ai
Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Helix request: tri-region dedicated capacity (staggered provisioning)

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Helix is excited about Redwood's performance, especially the lower P95 latency for medium-context chat. We’ve sketched out a demand plan for Q4 and want to propose a staggered provisioning approach so we can limit upfront financial commitment while still guaranteeing runway across US/EU/APAC.

High level asks:
- Initial committed pool: 40x A100-equivalent GPUs in US for 60 days (canonical traffic).
- Follow-on regional bursts: EU 20x and APAC 10x to be on standby, with 72-hour provisioning SLA once activated.
- Canary: route 5% of prod traffic to a EU canary two weeks after go-live.

Attached: Helix_demand_profile_Q4.xlsx (monthly token forecast + peak windows).

Can Redwood provide a recommended staggered provisioning playbook (sizing, gating conditions, canary cadence, fallback model variants) and a draft commercial term for a phased commit? We’d also like to understand how Dedicated vs. Dedicated+burst would affect pricing and SLAs.

We’re targeting a signed MOU by mid-November. Let me know if you want a sync this week.

Best,
Sara Nakamura
Head of Platform Integrations
Helix AI

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Helix request: tri-region dedicated capacity (staggered provisioning)

Team — forwarding Helix's ask. They want a playbook and phased commercial terms to avoid a big upfront commit. Key constraints: 72-hour regional provision SLA for EU/APAC bursts, 5% canary routing, target MOU by ~2026-11-15.

Can each of you take the sections below?
- Marissa: sizing + impact on pool fragmentation (what does 40/20/10 look like across our instance types and quantized variants).
- Karthik: recommended gating triggers (traffic thresholds, error budget burn, latency regressions) and fallbacks (model variant downgrade; regional fallback mapping).
- Ben: commercial framing — phased commit options (month-to-month tranche vs guaranteed minimums + burst billing) and the pricing delta for Dedicated+burst.

Deliverable: a short playbook PDF (2–3 pages) + an estimate spreadsheet we can share with Helix by EOD Tue (2026-10-27). If you need more time, propose a realistic deadline.

Thanks — Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Principal Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 11:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Helix request: tri-region dedicated capacity (staggered provisioning)

Aisha — quick sizing stub attached. I ran Helix's monthly peak token curves through our utilization model and produced a conservative GPU-equivalent footprint. Notes below: 

- Baseline (committed): 40x A100-eq in US covers steady-state + 30% headroom for daily peaks (approx. 1.2B tokens/day sustained).
- EU standby: 20x A100-eq with a cold-start profile (KV warm-up ~6h if no prefix cache). If we maintain 72-hr provisioning SLA, plan for pre-warming strategies (image snapshot + cache seeding on request).
- APAC standby: 10x A100-eq targeted to Singapore region; if Helix can accept a 24–48hr ramp for non-critical endpoints we could reduce committed reserve to 6x.

Tradeoffs: fragmentation increases cross-deal overhead; small regional pools hurt bin-packing efficiency and push higher unit costs. For that reason, our recommended playbook includes: 
- Staggered provisioning timeline: US commit day 0; EU canary day +14 (5% traffic), EU full ramp day +21, APAC ramp day +28 (unless earlier activation).
- Cache-warm strategy: snapshot KV caches for their common prefixes and a short-lived pre-warm window on activation to reduce P95 blowups.
- Fallback mapping: if EU pool is unavailable, route EU traffic to US dedicated with additional latency buffer and autoscaling policy to prioritize customer-critical requests.

I attached capacity_sizing_estimates.csv and a quick slide (staggered_playbook_v1.pdf). Questions: do we want to recommend a minimum burst credit pool (shared across regions) to minimize per-region idle capacity? That could lower their committed cap but increase burst pricing.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Helix request: tri-region dedicated capacity (staggered provisioning)

Thanks Marissa — nice work. A few gating and ops items I recommend adding to the playbook: 

- Gating triggers (activate next tranche):
  * sustained 7-day rolling avg token consumption > 85% of current committed capacity OR
  * spike event where 95th percentile token rate for 12 hours exceeds threshold AND error budget remaining < 10%
- Canary cadence: 5% traffic for 14 days, collect: latency percentiles, hallucination rate (from their eval set), and cost-per-successful-inference. If any of latency or hallucination regressions > 15% vs baseline, pause ramp.
- Autoscaling knobs: prefer larger step autoscale (20% increments) in EU/APAC to avoid oscillation; maintain a minimal per-GPU slot reservation for critical routes to preserve tail latency.
- Operational fallback: pre-authorized fallback allowance — allow routing up to 10% of EU traffic to US for up to 72 hours with predefined cost-sharing; document network egress implications.

I added these to the draft playbook (see Drive link). Also flagged GCP quota snapshot; Helix needs to confirm quotas for regional images and IP addresses before we commit to 72-hr SLA.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Capacity Planning & Infrastructure Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Helix request: tri-region dedicated capacity (staggered provisioning)

Sara — thanks for the detailed ask and the planning doc. Attached is a 2-page playbook and the sizing worksheet we discussed (staggered_playbook_v1.pdf; capacity_sizing_estimates.csv). High-level commitment:

- Redwood can support a phased approach: US committed 40x A100-eq on day 0; EU standby 20x and APAC standby 10x with activation SLAs as discussed.
- Commercial options: 1) 3-tranche monthly commits (lowest up-front) or 2) 60-day minimum for US + burst credits for regional standby (mid-line price). Ben will follow up with the specific quote and redlines.

Next steps:
- Ben to send formal commercial term sheet by EOD Wed (2026-11-04).
- Joint ops: Helix to confirm regional GCP quotas and provide a short prefix list for cache seeding by 2026-11-07.
- Technical sync scheduled: Wed 2026-11-10 09:00 PT (inv to follow).

Would you like us to summarize the gating triggers in the MOU or keep them in the separate Ops Annex? Both are fine but ops prefers Annex.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Principal Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
